Comment: Stage 1: moderate the photo, then use the vision guess as a food gate before spending anything on restaurant lookup or menu fetch. A non-food photo stops here and nothing downstream runs. If it is food, identify the restaurant and its menu, then match the guess against the real menu. Stops at Identified - recipe generation is a separate, user-triggered state machine.

ModerateImage.Comment: First and alone. Everything below costs money, so a rejected photo costs one moderation call and no model spend at all.

MarkJobRejected.Comment: A rejected photo is a normal terminal outcome, not an execution failure - hence Succeed rather than Fail. The reason is written for the user and shown in the app.

VisionGuess.Comment: The cheap food gate, run before any restaurant lookup or menu fetch. A non-food photo (pills, a pet, a landscape, an empty plate) costs one vision call and no restaurant/menu spend - the same first-and-alone discipline moderation uses one step up. It is sequential rather than parallel with the menu branch on purpose: a wasted paid menu fetch on a non-food photo is not worth the few seconds of overlap it would save on the happy path.

IsFood.Comment: The food gate. A non-food photo is a normal terminal outcome, not a failure, so it skips restaurant lookup, the menu fetch and the match, and ends like a moderation rejection.

MarkJobNotFood.Comment: Not a dish. Marked Failed for the user with a friendly reason, but ended rather than Failed - the same normal-terminal-outcome shape as MarkJobRejected.

HasSelectedRestaurant.Comment: The user either shared GPS or picked a restaurant by name - never both, which POST /api/jobs enforces.

HasCandidate.Comment: No restaurant near those coordinates is a valid outcome, not an error - it produces the vision-only low-confidence match downstream.

FetchRestaurantMenu.Comment: The activity already degrades a menu-fetch failure to an empty menu internally, so a task-level failure here is an infra hiccup, not a menu miss. Retry once only - each real attempt can run a paid SerpApi search plus an extract call, so a higher count risks re-billing it.

MatchMenuItem.Comment: The anti-hallucination step - a real menu item's name and description are trusted over the vision model's unaided guess. Records which of the three confidence outcomes occurred.

PersistMatchResult.Comment: vision_guess is persisted alongside the match because stage 2 takes it as input - nothing else records it until a recipe exists.

MarkJobFailed.Comment: Terminal failure for stage 1. Fail (not Succeed) so the execution shows as failed in the console and in CloudWatch metrics.

IdentifyFailed.Cause: Stage 1 failed; the job has been marked Failed with the underlying error.
